title: Employee Payroll Calculator
prompt: Build Employee Payroll Calculator: create a small Java implementation that demonstrates inheritance, polymorphism. Keep the design focused, validate input, and make normal and edge behavior observable. Use the acceptance criteria as the contract rather than matching a single hard-coded sample.
objective: Demonstrate inheritance, polymorphism in a maintainable Java program and explain the design choices.

starter.notes: Compiling scaffold only; implement the requirements in the prompt. Do not submit the TODO scaffold unchanged.

acceptance_criteria: The solution compiles on the stated JDK or documents why a version-specific feature is required.
The implementation demonstrates inheritance, polymorphism with clear names and focused methods.
Invalid or boundary input has defined behavior and does not silently corrupt the result.
At least three cases are tested and their expected outcomes are recorded.
The learner documents setup, run steps, and one limitation or trade-off.
hints: Write down the input, output, and domain rule before choosing data structures.
Implement the smallest working path and add one boundary case.
Separate parsing, domain logic, and output so each part can be tested.
grading_method: The current CodeLeaf grader supports a server-side required-token smoke check for this exercise. Passing it is not proof of correctness; apply the acceptance rubric and run tests, including hidden tests, before treating the work as verified.
retry_policy: Allow retries. Only a server-side correct grading result can complete the exercise; CodeLeaf applies XP once per activity and the course does not define XP.
status_note: Draft challenge with task-specific protected reference implementation notes; required-token grading is a smoke check, not proof of behavioral correctness. Review and add execution-based tests before publication.

test_cases.name: normal case
test_cases.purpose: Verify the principal behavior with typical input or synthetic data.

test_cases.name: boundary case
test_cases.purpose: Verify a documented boundary, empty collection, range limit, or concurrent completion condition.
test_cases.expected_behavior: Matches the declared contract and does not rely on undefined ordering.

test_cases.name: invalid or failure case
test_cases.purpose: Verify malformed input, absent resources, invalid configuration, or an external failure.
test_cases.expected_behavior: Produces a clear error or safe fallback; no credentials or private data are disclosed.

execution_notes: Java requires a local JDK or a separately isolated Java runner. This package does not add a runner; never execute arbitrary learner code inside the FastAPI process or the public web container.
